prompt: Research the EU AI Act's requirements for AI systems that use local model inference. Specifically investigate: (1) risk classification for local-first AI agents, (2) transparency requirements for systems using small language models, (3) data governance obligations when all inference happens on-device, and (4) any exemptions or reduced requirements for open-source AI systems. Cite official EU sources and legal analyses.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Legal requirements cited match the actual EU AI Act text and official guidance

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All four requested dimensions covered with specific article references

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites official EU legislation, regulatory guidance, or reputable legal analyses

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Provides actionable guidance for a local-first AI system developer, not just legal text dumps

prompt: Research and compare inference performance of small language models (1-8B parameters) across Apple Silicon generations (M1, M2, M3, M4). For each chip, find: (1) tokens/second for 4B models at Q8_0 quantization, (2) memory bandwidth and its impact on inference speed, (3) maximum model size that fits in unified memory for each RAM tier (16GB, 24GB, 32GB). Include data from llama.cpp benchmarks, MLX benchmarks, or community benchmarks. Cite all sources.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Benchmark numbers match cited sources, memory specs are correct for each chip

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All four chip generations covered with all three requested metrics

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites actual benchmark results, not speculation — from llama.cpp issues, MLX docs, or reputable tech publications

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Includes a comparative analysis with clear recommendations, not just raw numbers

prompt: Research current patterns for orchestrating multiple API calls in AI agent systems. Compare at least 4 approaches: (1) sequential chaining, (2) DAG-based parallel execution, (3) event-driven/reactive pipelines, (4) speculative execution with rollback. For each, find real-world implementations, analyze failure modes, and assess which patterns work best for unreliable tool calls (network failures, rate limits, partial results). Cite sources from engineering blogs, academic papers, or open-source projects.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Pattern descriptions match cited implementations, failure mode analysis is technically sound

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All four patterns covered with real implementations, failure modes, and suitability analysis

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites real engineering blogs, papers, or open-source repos — not fabricated references

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Comparative analysis with clear winner per use case, not just a feature list

prompt: Research and compare communication protocols used for AI agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent communication. Compare: (1) Model Context Protocol (MCP) from Anthropic, (2) OpenAI function calling / tool use, (3) LangChain tool abstraction, (4) Google A2A (Agent-to-Agent), and (5) any emerging standards. For each, analyze: wire format, capability negotiation, streaming support, error handling semantics, and extensibility. Assess which is most suitable for local-first systems where latency matters. Cite official documentation and technical specifications.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Protocol specifications match official documentation — wire formats, capability models, error semantics

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All five protocols covered with all five requested dimensions

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites official specs, SDK docs, and technical RFCs — not blog summaries

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Clear recommendation for local-first use case with supporting rationale, head-to-head comparison table

prompt: Research the current licensing landscape for distributing AI applications that embed or bundle open-weight language models. Cover: (1) Meta's Llama license terms and commercial use restrictions, (2) Qwen's license for the Qwen-3.5 family, (3) Google's Gemma license, (4) Mistral's licensing model, (5) the RAIL license family (BigScience, BigCode). For each, analyze: commercial use permissions, modification rights, redistribution rules, attribution requirements, and any use-case restrictions. Identify which licenses are compatible with bundling a model inside a commercial desktop application. Cite official license texts and legal analyses.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: License terms match the actual official license texts — not outdated or misinterpreted

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All five license families covered with all five requested dimensions

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites official license texts from model repos, not third-party summaries

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Clear compatibility matrix for commercial desktop bundling use case, actionable legal guidance
